cities.name: Khajuraho
cities.overview: A small town in Chhatarpur district built around India's most celebrated group of medieval Hindu and Jain temples.

cities.name: Sanchi
cities.overview: A hilltop village in Raisen district, about 45 km from Bhopal, crowned by the oldest stone structures in India.

cities.name: Bhopal
cities.overview: Madhya Pradesh's capital, the City of Lakes, and a base for Sanchi and the rock shelters of Bhimbetka.
cities.history: Founded in the early 18th century by the Afghan soldier Dost Mohammad Khan. It was ruled for over a century by a remarkable line of women, the Begums of Bhopal.

cities.name: Kanha
cities.overview: The forest country of Mandla and Balaghat districts, with lodges clustered around the Kisli, Mukki and Khatia gates of Kanha Tiger Reserve.

cities.name: Indore
cities.overview: Madhya Pradesh's largest city, an old Holkar capital with a famous street food market at Sarafa.
cities.history: Built up under the Holkars of the Maratha empire, most famously under the queen Ahilyabai Holkar's rule. It's now the commercial capital of the state.

cities.name: Gwalior
cities.overview: A city under one of India's greatest hill forts, and a long-standing centre of Hindustani classical music.
cities.history: Ruled over the centuries by the Tomars, the Mughals and finally the Scindia family of the Marathas, who made it a princely capital in the 18th century.

cities.name: Ujjain
cities.overview: One of Hinduism's seven sacred cities, on the Shipra River, host of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela.

cities.name: Orchha
cities.overview: A small town of Bundela palaces and cenotaphs on the Betwa River.

cities.name: Jabalpur
cities.overview: A city on the Narmada, the base for the Marble Rocks and for Kanha and Bandhavgarh.

cities.name: Mandu
cities.overview: A ruined Afghan city on a plateau in the Malwa hills, spread out above the Narmada plain.

cities.name: Maheshwar
cities.overview: A town on the Narmada, with a fort and ghats from the reign of Ahilyabai Holkar, and a name for its handloom saris.

cities.name: Pachmarhi
cities.overview: The hill station of Madhya Pradesh, in the Satpura Range, among forests, waterfalls and cave shelters.

cities.name: Umaria
cities.overview: A forest-district town, the rail gateway for Bandhavgarh.

cities.name: Amarkantak
cities.overview: A hill town where the Vindhyas meet the Satpuras, and the source of the Narmada.

cities.name: Sheopur
cities.overview: A town near the Chambal, close to Kuno National Park.

cities.name: Ashoknagar
cities.overview: A district town in northern Madhya Pradesh and the base for Chanderi.

cities.name: Khandwa
cities.overview: A Nimar town, the rail head for the island temple of Omkareshwar.

places.name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
places.shortDescription: UNESCO-listed Chandela temples famed for their soaring spires and intricate, often sensual, sculpture.
places.description: About 25 of the original 85 temples at Khajuraho survive, grouped into Western, Eastern and Southern clusters. The Western Group, inside a landscaped ASI enclosure, holds the masterpieces: Kandariya Mahadeva, Lakshmana and Vishvanatha, their walls crowded with gods, dancers, warriors and the erotic couples that made Khajuraho famous. The Eastern Group includes elegant Jain temples. The evening sound-and-light show and the Khajuraho Dance Festival in February are highlights.
places.history: The temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between about 950 and 1050 CE. Hidden by forest for centuries, they were brought to wider notice by British surveyor T. S. Burt in 1838 and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. The Khajuraho Dance Festival is held in February.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates for the Western Group (slightly less online); verify before your visit.

location.address: Western Group of Temples, Khajuraho, Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh 471606

highlights: Jain temples of the Eastern Group

places.name: Sanchi Stupa
places.shortDescription: The Great Stupa begun by Emperor Ashoka, with four exquisitely carved stone gateways.
places.description: Sanchi's hilltop holds stupas, monasteries, temples and pillars spanning more than a thousand years of Buddhist history. The Great Stupa is ringed by four toranas, gateways carved with Jataka tales and scenes from the Buddha's life in which the Buddha himself appears only as symbols such as a footprint, a wheel or a tree. The ASI museum at the foot of the hill displays the lion capital of Ashoka's pillar found here. It is an easy day trip from Bhopal.
places.history: The emperor Ashoka commissioned the first brick stupa in the 3rd century BCE; it was enlarged in stone and the gateways added around the 1st century BCE. The monuments were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates (slightly less online); verify before your visit.

places.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
places.shortDescription: Rock shelters with prehistoric paintings, some of the oldest traces of human life in India.
places.description: In the forested Vindhya foothills south of Bhopal, hundreds of sandstone rock shelters hold paintings of hunters, dancers, horses, elephants and bison in red and white pigments. A paved trail leads past the most striking shelters, including the vast Auditorium Cave and the Zoo Rock with its crowded animal scenes. The paintings span from the Mesolithic to the medieval period. The site is about 45 km from Bhopal.
places.history: The shelters were brought to scholarly attention by archaeologist V. S. Wakankar in 1957. They were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; mornings are best for light and temperature.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates plus a vehicle fee; verify before your visit.

places.name: Kanha Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: Sal forests and meadows that saved the hard-ground barasingha and offer some of India's best tiger safaris.
places.description: Kanha's mix of sal forest, bamboo and open meadows supports tigers, leopards, gaur, wild dogs and the hard-ground barasingha, a swamp deer found nowhere else and brought back from the brink here. Jeep safaris run from the Kisli, Mukki, Khatia and Sarhi gates, and permits should be booked online well ahead. Bamni Dadar plateau offers sunset views over the forest. The landscape is often said to have inspired Kipling's Jungle Book.
places.history: Kanha was declared a national park in 1955 and became one of the first tiger reserves under Project Tiger in 1973. Its conservation of the barasingha is one of India's wildlife success stories.
places.bestTimeNote: November to May (summer gives the best tiger sightings). Core zones are closed from 1 July to 15 October.

entryFee.note: Safari permits are booked online on the MP Forest Department portal; prices vary by zone and vehicle.

location.address: Kanha Tiger Reserve, Mandla district, Madhya Pradesh 481768

places.name: Taj-ul-Masajid
places.shortDescription: One of the largest mosques in India, in pink stone with white domes, in the old city of Bhopal.
places.description: Huge courtyard, tall minarets and a capacity of about 26,000 worshippers. Its name means the Crown of Mosques, and it's still an active seat of learning.
places.history: Started by Shah Jahan Begum in the 19th century, and finished only in the 1980s.

places.name: Upper Lake, Bhopal
places.shortDescription: Bhojtal, a large old lake on the western side of Bhopal, the source of 40% of the city's water.
places.description: A huge lake at the edge of the city, with boat rides, and Van Vihar along the south bank. The sunset from the VIP Road is a Bhopal favourite.
places.history: Traditionally linked to the Paramara king Bhoja in the 11th century.

places.name: Van Vihar National Park
places.shortDescription: A national park that's run like a zoo in Bhopal, with rescued animals along the Upper Lake.
places.description: A small park of 4.45 sq km, with a road for walkers, cyclists and cars to pass by the open enclosures of tigers, lions and bears.
places.history: Declared a national park in 1979.

places.name: Bhojeshwar Temple
places.shortDescription: An unfinished 11th-century Shiva temple at Bhojpur, with a 7.5-foot lingam in its sanctum.
places.description: An incomplete temple of huge pillars, and a rare look at how such a place was built. Plans carved on nearby rocks and the earth ramp are still visible.
places.history: Traditionally attributed to the Paramara king Bhoja, in the 11th century.

places.name: Udayagiri Caves
places.shortDescription: Twenty rock-cut caves near Vidisha, with some of the oldest surviving Hindu sculptures in India.
places.description: A low hill near Vidisha, with a giant Varaha panel showing Vishnu as a boar. It's quiet and just a short way from the crowds at Sanchi.
places.history: Carved in the Gupta period, from the early 3rd to the 5th century CE.

places.name: Gwalior Fort
places.shortDescription: A huge hill fort that Babur called the pearl amongst the fortresses of Hind.
places.description: Blue-tiled Man Singh Palace, Sas-Bahu temples and giant rock-cut Jain figures, all spread along a long plateau.
places.history: Its history reaches back at least to the 6th century. The Tomar king Man Singh built its greatest palace.

places.name: Jai Vilas Palace
places.shortDescription: An 1874 palace of the Scindias, with two of the largest chandeliers in the world.
places.description: A huge European-style palace, part of it a museum. A silver toy train carried drinks around the dining table, and it's still on show.
places.history: Built in 1874 by Jayajirao Scindia, the Maharaja of Gwalior.

places.name: Bateshwar Temples
places.shortDescription: About 200 sandstone temples in the Morena hills, north of Gwalior, restored from ruin.
places.description: Rows of small post-Gupta temples, on a quiet hillside, that were pieced back together by archaeologists after being found in ruins.
places.history: Built in the post-Gupta, early Gurjara-Pratihara period.

places.name: Kuno National Park
places.shortDescription: A national park in the Gwalior Chambal region, known for India's cheetah reintroduction project.
places.description: Dry forest and grassland along the Kuno River. India's cheetah project brought African cheetahs here from 2022, and safaris are now open.
places.history: Established in 1981 as a wildlife sanctuary.

places.name: Chanderi
places.shortDescription: A historic town in the Vindhyas, known for its handwoven saris, fort and old mosques.
places.description: A small town of Sultanate gates and mosques, with a tall fort and active handlooms. It's a good place to buy Chanderi silk.

places.name: Jahangir Mahal
places.shortDescription: A vast Bundela palace in Orchha, built for the Mughal emperor Jahangir's visit.
places.description: Domed pavilions, carved windows and rooftop views of the Betwa. It's the finest building in the Orchha fort complex.
places.history: Raja Bir Singh Deo built it to mark Jahangir's visit in the 17th century.

places.name: Orchha Fort Complex
places.shortDescription: An island fort on the Betwa River, with three palaces, gardens and royal halls.
places.description: A set of palaces and temples reached by a bridge. Raj Mahal has fine murals, and the evening light on the Betwa cenotaphs is lovely.
places.history: The Bundela ruler Rudra Pratap Singh made Orchha his capital in the 16th century.

places.name: Mahakaleshwar Temple
places.shortDescription: A Shiva Jyotirlinga on the Shipra in Ujjain, known for its pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti.
places.description: One of the twelve holiest Shiva shrines, with a south-facing lingam. The Mahakal Lok corridor now leads pilgrims in, and you need to book the dawn aarti ahead.

places.name: Rajwada
places.shortDescription: The 200-year-old Holkar palace at the centre of Indore, with a seven-storey gate.
places.description: A blend of Maratha, Mughal and French styles, right in the middle of the bazaar. The evening food market at Sarafa is only a few minutes away.
places.history: Built by the Holkars around two centuries ago.

places.name: Lalbagh Palace
places.shortDescription: The grand Holkar palace on the Khan River in Indore, with European-style rooms.
places.description: A palace of Italian marble and Greek-style halls, a sharp contrast with Rajwada. Its gates are modelled on Buckingham Palace.
places.history: Built by the Holkar dynasty between 1886 and 1921.

places.name: Omkareshwar
places.shortDescription: An island Jyotirlinga temple on the Narmada, in an island shaped like the sacred syllable Om.
places.description: A white temple high above the river on Mandhata island, reached by bridge or boat. A giant statue of Adi Shankara now stands on the hill.
places.history: One of the twelve revered Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.

places.name: Maheshwar Fort and Ghats
places.shortDescription: Ahilyabai Holkar's fort, ghats and temples on the Narmada, the setting for many Hindi films.
places.description: Stone ghats and temples rise from the river, with the fort above. The Rehwa handloom weavers work in the fort, and the sunset boats are lovely.
places.history: The Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar made it her capital in the 18th century.

places.name: Mandu
places.shortDescription: A ruined Afghan city on a plateau in Malwa, with the Jahaz Mahal, a palace shaped like a ship.
places.description: Palaces, mosques and tombs are spread across the green plateau. Don't miss the ship-like Jahaz Mahal, Hoshang Shah's marble tomb and Rani Roopmati's Pavilion.
places.history: It was the capital of the Malwa sultans, and is the setting of the love story of Baz Bahadur and Roopmati.

places.name: Pachmarhi
places.shortDescription: Satpura ki Rani, a green plateau hill station with waterfalls, caves and old church towers.
places.description: Waterfalls, forest walks and rock paintings in a British-era cantonment. Bee Falls and Dhupgarh, the highest point in the region, are favourites.

places.name: Satpura Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A rugged tiger reserve in Narmadapuram, known for walking and canoe safaris.
places.description: One of the few reserves in India where you can explore on foot or by canoe. Sloth bears and leopards live in sal forests and sandstone hills.

places.name: Bandhavgarh National Park
places.shortDescription: A national park in Umaria with one of India's highest densities of tigers and an old hill fort.
places.description: Sal forest and rocky hills around the ruined Bandhavgarh Fort. It's probably the best place in India to see a tiger, particularly in the Tala zone.
places.history: Declared a national park in 1968, and a tiger reserve in 1993.

places.name: Panna National Park
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve near Khajuraho, with gorges and the Ken River, where tigers were brought back.
places.description: Rocky plateau and gorges along the Ken River, a short drive from Khajuraho. Tigers disappeared by 2009 and were successfully brought back.
places.history: Declared India's 22nd tiger reserve in 1994.

places.name: Marble Rocks, Bhedaghat
places.shortDescription: White marble cliffs along the Narmada near Jabalpur, seen by boat, best under the moon.
places.description: The river runs for kilometres through a gorge of shining white and blue marble cliffs. Boat rides are the thing to do, and they run under the moon on some nights.

places.name: Dhuandhar Falls
places.shortDescription: A foggy waterfall on the Narmada near Bhedaghat, and the river's most dramatic drop.
places.description: The Narmada crashes down in a thick smoke of spray, giving the falls their name. A cable car crosses right above it.

places.name: Narmada Udgam, Amarkantak
places.shortDescription: The source of the Narmada, in a holy tank in the temple town of Amarkantak.
places.description: A small white temple complex marks where the Narmada begins, and nearby are old Kalachuri temples, along with the falls at Kapildhara.
